literal: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai
idiomatic: Xiao Ming; Xiao Zhi; Xiao Tui; Xiao Fang; Xu Zhicai

literal: Xiao Ming was a man of Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, the Liang emperor Wu's eldest brother's son.
idiomatic: Xiao Ming was from Lanling, son of Prince of Changsha Yi, eldest brother of Emperor Wu of Liang.

literal: In his own dynasty he was greatly beloved by Liang Wu.
idiomatic: In his own court he was greatly beloved by Emperor Wu of Liang.

literal: In youth he passed through eminent offices and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.
idiomatic: In youth he held eminent posts and was enfeoffed Marquis of Zhenyang.

literal: In the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.
idiomatic: During the Taiqing era he was made inspector of Yuzhou.

literal: After the Liang ruler had accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng, with a grand design of advance.
idiomatic: After the Liang ruler accepted Hou Jing, an edict ordered Ming to lead land and river forces toward Pengcheng for a major advance.

literal: He also ordered Yanzhou inspector Heir Prince of Nankang Hui Li to command all commanders and assign strategy.
idiomatic: He also ordered Yanzhou inspector Heir Prince of Nankang Hui Li to take overall command of the generals and set strategy.

literal: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took all his host captive.
idiomatic: Ming had crossed the Huai only a short while when the government army defeated him and took his entire force captive.

literal: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower and personally received Ming and the generals, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.
idiomatic: The Wei emperor ascended the gate tower, received Ming and the generals in person, released their bonds, and sent them to Jinyang.

literal: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him: "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng treated Ming with great courtesy and said to him, "The late king and the Liang ruler were on good terms for more than ten years; I heard that when he performed Buddhist rites he would say he did them for the Wei ruler and for the late king as well—this was truly the Liang ruler's great kindness.

literal: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.
idiomatic: Who would have thought that in a single morning faith would be broken and bring this turmoil.

literal: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.
idiomatic: Since our armies went forth on a light campaign, there has been no battle we did not win, no city we did not take; now that we ourselves wish peace, it is not because our strength is spent.

literal: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.
idiomatic: Matters on the border—I know they are not the Liang ruler's true intent; surely Hou Jing defied orders and stirred this up.

literal: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once.
idiomatic: You may send envoys to consult; if he still honors the late king's bond and restores friendly relations, I need not go against the late king's wish—you and the others will all be released at once.

literal: " Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.
idiomatic: " Thereupon he had men report to the Liang ruler with Ming's letter; the Liang ruler then sent a letter in reply to comfort Gao Cheng.

literal: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Tianbao, when Emperor Yuan of Liang was destroyed by Western Wei, Gao Yang issued an edict installing Ming as Liang ruler; Liang generals previously captured, such as Zhan Haizhen, were all allowed to follow Ming home, and Prince of Shangdang Huan was ordered to lead troops to escort them.

literal: At that time Liang Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian and Minister of Works Chen Baxian were at Jiankang; they installed Prince of Jin'an Fang Zhi as chancellor.
idiomatic: At that time Liang grand commandant Wang Sengbian and minister of works Chen Baxian were at Jiankang; they installed Prince of Jin'an Fang Zhi as chancellor.

literal: Gao Yang bestowed sealed letters on Sengbian and Baxian; Sengbian did not obey the edict.
idiomatic: Gao Yang bestowed sealed letters on Sengbian and Baxian; Sengbian did not obey the edict.

literal: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.
idiomatic: Prince of Shangdang advanced his army; Ming also exchanged letters with Sengbian back and forth several times, setting out fortune and calamity, but at first Sengbian would not accept him.

literal: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.
idiomatic: Then Prince of Shangdang broke Dongguan and beheaded Pei Zhiheng; the lands south of the Yangtze were gripped with fear, and Sengbian then memorialized Prince of Shangdang asking to admit Ming and sent warships to receive him.

literal: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.
idiomatic: The prince feasted Liang officers and men and, with Ming, slaughtered a victim and drank the blood, loading the covenant onto a chariot.

literal: Thereupon the Liang carriage went east across the river and the Qi army turned north.
idiomatic: Thereupon the Liang carriage went east across the river and the Qi army turned north.

literal: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Chao, and the like were not within the amnesty.
idiomatic: Palace attendant Pei Yingqi guarded and escorted Ming into Jiankang; he then assumed the imperial title, changed the fourth year of Chengsheng to the first year of Tiancheng, and proclaimed a general amnesty—Yuwen Heitu, the rebel Chao, and the like were not within the amnesty.

literal: Fang Zhi was made heir apparent; Wang Sengbian was appointed grand marshal.
idiomatic: Fang Zhi was made heir apparent; Wang Sengbian was appointed grand marshal.

literal: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang Chi to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.
idiomatic: Ming submitted a memorial sending his second son Zhang Chi to the capital to bow in thanks before the palace.

literal: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.
idiomatic: In winter Baxian attacked and killed Sengbian, restored Fang Zhi, and made Ming grand tutor and Prince of Jian'an.

literal: Baxian submitted a memorial to the court saying Sengbian had plotted treason in secret and was therefore executed.
idiomatic: Baxian submitted a memorial to the court saying Sengbian had plotted treason in secret and was therefore executed.

literal: Fang Zhi asked to style himself subject and remain a vassal state forever; Qi sent acting commissioner Sima Gong and Liang men to covenant at Liyang.
idiomatic: Fang Zhi asked to style himself subject and remain a vassal state forever; Qi sent acting commissioner Sima Gong and Liang men to covenant at Liyang.

literal: The next year an edict summoned Ming.
idiomatic: The next year an edict summoned Ming.

literal: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.
idiomatic: Baxian still styled himself vassal and was about to send envoys to deliver Ming, but Ming died of a carbuncle on his back.

literal: Liang general Wang Lin on the river resisted Baxian; Gao Yang sent troops to install Liang Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang to uphold the Liang succession.
idiomatic: Liang general Wang Lin on the river resisted Baxian; Gao Yang sent troops to install Liang Prince of Yongjia Xiao Zhuang to uphold the Liang succession.

literal: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.
idiomatic: In the second month of the ninth year he crossed the river from Pencheng; in the third month he took the throne at Yingzhou, era name Tianqi; Wang Lin directed state and army; posthumous title for Ming was Emperor Min.

literal: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men and then entered court; he was enfeoffed marquis.
idiomatic: The next year Zhuang was defeated by Chen men and then entered court; he was enfeoffed marquis.

literal: The court had promised restoration, but in the end it did not come to pass.
idiomatic: The court had promised restoration, but in the end it did not come to pass.

literal: On the day the Last Lord perished, Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.
idiomatic: On the day the Last Lord perished, Zhuang died in Ye from pent-up grief.

literal: Xiao Zhi, style Jingshi, was son of Liang Wu's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.
idiomatic: Xiao Zhi, style Jingshi, was son of Emperor Wu of Liang's younger brother Prince of Nanping Wei.

literal: In youth he was clever and keen, with fine looks.
idiomatic: In youth he was clever and keen, with fine looks.

literal: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and held the post of eastern Yangzhou inspector.
idiomatic: In Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Dingxiang and held the post of eastern Yangzhou inspector.

literal: At that time the lands east of the Yangtze were at peace; government was lax and people grew slack—Zhi alone governed with severity, and Liang Wu was pleased.
idiomatic: At that time the lands east of the Yangtze were at peace; government was lax and people grew slack—Zhi alone governed with severity, and Emperor Wu of Liang was pleased.

literal: He was transferred to northern Yanzhou inspector.
idiomatic: He was transferred to northern Yanzhou inspector.

literal: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jiankang.
idiomatic: In the second year of Taiqing, Hou Jing besieged Jiankang.

literal: Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came to surrender.
idiomatic: Zhi heard the capital had fallen and came to surrender.

literal: In the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye; Gao Cheng had Wei Shou and Xing Shao meet and converse with him.
idiomatic: In the seventh year of Wuding he reached Ye; Gao Cheng had Wei Shou and Xing Shao meet and converse with him.

literal: He passed through the posts of heir apparent junior tutor and tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe commandery.
idiomatic: He passed through the posts of heir apparent junior tutor and tutor to Prince of Pingyang, and was enfeoffed Duke of Qinghe commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made Right Bright Light Grand Master and director of the Imperial University.
idiomatic: At the beginning of Qi Tianbao he was made right bright light grand master and director of the imperial university.

literal: When Emperor Yuan of Liang had pacified Hou Jing and renewed friendly relations with Qi, Gao Yang wished to release Zhi and the others to return south.
idiomatic: When Emperor Yuan of Liang had pacified Hou Jing and renewed friendly relations with Qi, Gao Yang wished to release Zhi and the others to return south.

literal: Before long Western Wei took Jiangling; he therefore remained at Ye and died.
idiomatic: Before long Western Wei took Jiangling; he therefore remained at Ye and died.

literal: Posthumous gifts: secretariat director, chariot and cavalry grand general, Yangzhou inspector.
idiomatic: Posthumous gifts: secretariat director, chariot and cavalry grand general, Yangzhou inspector.

literal: Xiao Tui was son of Liang emperor Wu's younger brother Minister of Works Prince of Poyang Hui.
idiomatic: Xiao Tui was son of Emperor Wu of Liang's younger brother minister of works Prince of Poyang Hui.

literal: In Liang Tui was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and held Qingzhou inspector.
idiomatic: In Liang Tui was enfeoffed Marquis of Xiangtan and held Qingzhou inspector.

literal: When Jiankang fell, he entered Eastern Wei together with his elder cousin Zhi.
idiomatic: When Jiankang fell, he entered Eastern Wei together with his elder cousin Zhi.

literal: In Qi Tianbao he held the post of golden purple light grand master and died.
idiomatic: In Qi Tianbao he held the post of golden purple light grand master and died.

literal: His son Kai was deep and reserved, courteous, fond of goodness and eager to learn, and skilled at cursive and clerical script.
idiomatic: His son Kai was deep and reserved, courteous, fond of goodness and eager to learn, and skilled at cursive and clerical script.

literal: Among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.
idiomatic: Among southern gentlemen he was called an elder.

literal: He passed through associate editor of the Historiography Office and attendant at Wenslin Hall, and died as aide to the director of the masters of writing.
idiomatic: He passed through associate editor of the historiography office and attendant at Wenslin Hall, and died as aide to the director of the masters of writing.

literal: Xiao Fang, style Xiyi, followed his father Zhi to Ye.
idiomatic: Xiao Fang, style Xiyi, followed his father Zhi to Ye.

literal: When Zhi died, Fang's mourning for him won fame for filial piety.
idiomatic: When Zhi died, Fang's mourning for him won fame for filial piety.

literal: Before the mourning hut two loving birds came and gathered; each took a tree for its nest; from before noon they were tame in the courtyard, drinking and pecking; after noon they no longer left the trees; whenever the hour came they spread their wings and cried mournfully, altogether like weeping in grief.
idiomatic: Before the mourning hut two loving birds came and gathered; each took a tree for its nest; from before noon they were tame in the courtyard, drinking and pecking; after noon they no longer left the trees; whenever the hour came they spread their wings and cried mournfully, altogether like weeping in grief.

literal: The household watched them and never found an absence.
idiomatic: The household watched them and never found an absence.

literal: People of the time took it as the response of utmost filial piety.
idiomatic: People of the time took it as the response of utmost filial piety.

literal: When mourning ended he inherited the title.
idiomatic: When mourning ended he inherited the title.

literal: In the Wuping era he was attendant at Wenslin Hall.
idiomatic: In the Wuping era he was attendant at Wenslin Hall.

literal: Fang by nature loved literary composition and was fairly skilled at painting; therefore in the palace he perused histories and recent poetry and rhapsodies, oversaw painters at work on screens and other miscellaneous objects, became known, and was favored.
idiomatic: Fang by nature loved literary composition and was fairly skilled at painting; therefore in the palace he perused histories and recent poetry and rhapsodies, oversaw painters at work on screens and other miscellaneous objects, became known, and was favored.

literal: He was promoted repeatedly to heir apparent attendant and attendant-in-ordinary.
idiomatic: He was promoted repeatedly to heir apparent attendant and attendant-in-ordinary.

literal: Xu Zhicai was a man of Danyang.
idiomatic: Xu Zhicai was a man of Danyang.

literal: His father Xiong served Southern Qi as administrator of Lanling and was famed in the lands east of the Yangtze for medical skill.
idiomatic: His father Xiong served Southern Qi as administrator of Lanling and was famed in the lands east of the Yangtze for medical skill.

literal: Zhicai in childhood was precocious; at five he recited the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he had a rough grasp of its meaning.
idiomatic: Zhicai in childhood was precocious; at five he recited the Classic of Filial Piety, and at eight he had a rough grasp of its meaning.

literal: Once he went with his elder cousin Kang to the house of Liang heir apparent's household chief Runan Zhou She to hear the Laozi.
idiomatic: Once he went with his elder cousin Kang to the house of Liang heir apparent's household chief Runan Zhou She to hear the Laozi.

literal: She set out food and then teased him, saying: "Master Xu, you do not apply your mind to meaning but only to eating?
idiomatic: She set out food and then teased him, saying, "Master Xu, you do not apply your mind to meaning but only to eating?

literal: " Zhicai answered: "I have heard that the sage empties his mind and fills his belly."
idiomatic: " Zhicai answered, "I have heard that the sage empties his mind and fills his belly."

literal: She sighed in admiration.
idiomatic: She sighed in admiration.

literal: At thirteen he was summoned as Imperial Academy student and had a rough mastery of the Rites and the Changes.
idiomatic: At thirteen he was summoned as imperial academy student and had a rough mastery of the Rites and the Changes.

literal: Pengcheng Liu Xiaochuo, Hedong Pei Ziye, Wu commandery Zhang Sheng, and others often debated the Book of Changes and mourning-garment ritual with him; his replies came like an echo.
idiomatic: Pengcheng Liu Xiaochuo, Hedong Pei Ziye, Wu commandery Zhang Sheng, and others often debated the Book of Changes and mourning-garment ritual with him; his replies came like an echo.

literal: They all sighed together: "This is a divine child."
idiomatic: They all sighed together, "This is a divine child."

literal: Xiaochuo also said: "Master Xu has a swallow jaw—he has the look of Ban Chao the Distance-Pacifier."
idiomatic: Xiaochuo also said, "Master Xu has a swallow jaw—he has the look of Ban Chao the Distance-Pacifier."

literal: Chen commandery Yuan Ang held Danyang prefect; he recruited Zhicai as chief clerk, and whenever men had business affairs they were all referred to him for counsel.
idiomatic: Chen commandery Yuan Ang held Danyang prefect; he recruited Zhicai as chief clerk, and whenever men had business affairs they were all referred to him for counsel.

literal: The prefectural offices suffered fire; Zhicai rose to look and in the night wore no clothes, but came out of the room in a red kerchief over his shoulders; the light caught him and Ang saw it.
idiomatic: The prefectural offices suffered fire; Zhicai rose to look and in the night wore no clothes, but came out of the room in a red kerchief over his shoulders; the light caught him and Ang saw it.

literal: The merit officer memorialized asking that he be dismissed; Ang valued his talent and skill and specially pardoned him.
idiomatic: The merit officer memorialized asking that he be dismissed; Ang valued his talent and skill and specially pardoned him.

literal: Prince of Yuzhang Zong went out to garrison Jiangdu; Zhicai was again made left regular attendant of the Yuzhang kingdom, then transferred to Zong's northern campaign chief clerk.
idiomatic: Prince of Yuzhang Zong went out to garrison Jiangdu; Zhicai was again made left regular attendant of the Yuzhang kingdom, then transferred to Zong's northern campaign chief clerk.

literal: When Zong entered Wei the three armies scattered and fled; Zhicai retreated to Lüliang; the bridge was cut and the road gone, and he was stopped by Wei commanding general Shi Maosun.
idiomatic: When Zong entered Wei the three armies scattered and fled; Zhicai retreated to Lüliang; the bridge was cut and the road gone, and he was stopped by Wei commanding general Shi Maosun.

literal: Within a month of Zong's entering Wei he reached the rank of minister of works.
idiomatic: Within a month of Zong's entering Wei he reached the rank of minister of works.

literal: Wei allowed Zong to gather his staff; he then inquired after Zhicai at Peng and Si and reported to the Wei emperor: "Zhicai is greatly skilled in medicine and also has ready wit."
idiomatic: Wei allowed Zong to gather his staff; he then inquired after Zhicai at Peng and Si and reported to the Wei emperor, "Zhicai is greatly skilled in medicine and also has ready wit."

literal: An edict summoned Zhicai.
idiomatic: An edict summoned Zhicai.

literal: In the second year of Xiaochang he reached Luoyang; he was ordered to lodge in the Southern Lodge and received very generous treatment.
idiomatic: In the second year of Xiaochang he reached Luoyang; he was ordered to lodge in the Southern Lodge and received very generous treatment.

literal: Cousin Zhan's son Jian memorialized asking that Zhicai return home.
idiomatic: Cousin Zhan's son Jian memorialized asking that Zhicai return home.

literal: Zhicai's medicines were often effective; he also dipped into the classics and histories; when he spoke he was sharp and quick; court worthies vied to invite him and spread his fame.
idiomatic: Zhicai's medicines were often effective; he also dipped into the classics and histories; when he spoke he was sharp and quick; court worthies vied to invite him and spread his fame.

literal: In the time of Emperor Wu he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.
idiomatic: In the time of Emperor Wu of Liang he was enfeoffed Marquis of Chang'an county.

literal: In the Tianping era Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang; he was constantly in the inner lodge and his treatment grew somewhat richer.
idiomatic: In the Tianping era Gao Huan summoned him to Jinyang; he was constantly in the inner lodge and his treatment grew somewhat richer.

literal: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from attendant-in-ordinary to secretariat director.
idiomatic: In the fourth year of Wuding he was transferred from attendant-in-ordinary to secretariat director.

literal: When Gao Yang became chancellor he promoted and demoted widely.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang became chancellor he promoted and demoted widely.

literal: Yang Yin, because he was a man of the southern lands and unfit to direct the secretariat, transferred him to golden purple light grand master and had Wei Shou replace him in that office.
idiomatic: Yang Yin, because he was a man of the southern lands and unfit to direct the secretariat, transferred him to golden purple light grand master and had Wei Shou replace him in that office.

literal: Zhicai was very resentful and displeased.
idiomatic: Zhicai was very resentful and displeased.

literal: Zhicai from youth understood astronomy and also the learning of prognostic texts; with lodge companion Song Jingye he compared auspice and ill omen and knew that in the wu year there would surely be change; he therefore reported this through Gao Dezheng.
idiomatic: Zhicai from youth understood astronomy and also the learning of prognostic texts; with lodge companion Song Jingye he compared auspice and ill omen and knew that in the wu year there would surely be change; he therefore reported this through Gao Dezheng.

literal: Gao Yang heard it and was greatly pleased.
idiomatic: Gao Yang heard it and was greatly pleased.

literal: At the time from Empress Dowager Lou down to meritorious ministers all said Guanxi was already a formidable foe and feared they would use the phrase of taking the Son of Heaven in hand to command the feudal lords—one must not first carry out the abdication.
idiomatic: At the time from Empress Dowager Lou down to meritorious ministers all said Guanxi was already a formidable foe and feared they would use the phrase of taking the Son of Heaven in hand to command the feudal lords—one must not first carry out the abdication.

literal: Zhicai alone said: "A thousand men chase a hare; when one man gets it, all the rest cease.
idiomatic: Zhicai alone said, "A thousand men chase a hare; when one man gets it, all the rest cease.

literal: The great enterprise must be settled—how can you turn about and wish to learn from others?"
idiomatic: The great enterprise must be settled—how can you turn about and wish to learn from others?"

literal: He also cited evidence, fully itemized; the emperor followed him.
idiomatic: He also cited evidence, fully itemized; the emperor followed him.

literal: After he ascended the throne, intimacy grew still closer.
idiomatic: After he ascended the throne, intimacy grew still closer.

literal: Zhicai advanced not only through medical skill; he was also foremost in urging the abdication, and again he jested with wit and buffoonery, speaking without reserve—therefore he was greatly favored and familiar.
idiomatic: Zhicai advanced not only through medical skill; he was also foremost in urging the abdication, and again he jested with wit and buffoonery, speaking without reserve—therefore he was greatly favored and familiar.
